newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Dole teams fail to meet on debates.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Dole teams fail to meet on debates.

text.p: The odds of the first presidential debate taking place next week appeared slimmer than ever Wednesday as negotiators for President Clinton and Republican Bob Dole failed to resume talks on the format.

Dole's chief negotiator, former South Carolina Gov. Carroll Campbell, spoke by telephone with Clinton's representative, Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor. But Campbell had a scheduling conflict that prevented them from meeting, spokesmen for both sides said.
The negotiating teams met on Tuesday for more than two hours but the session ended with no resolution of outstanding issues such as how many debates and how long they should be.

A major point of contention was whether third party candidate Ross Perot should be excluded as the Commission on Presidential Debates recommended on Tuesday. The Clinton forces want Perot, the Dole forces do not.
Officials in both the Clinton and Dole campaigns said it might be the weekend before their negotiators finally met and each suggested the delay was the other side's fault.
"Our negotiators said that the Dole people seemed ill-prepared for yesterday's events and there seemed to have been some disagreement within their group," a Clinton campaign official said.

He said Kantor and other members of the Democratic negotiating team had been ready to meet on Wednesday afternoon but that Campbell and the other Republicans had asked for a 36-hour delay before the next session. "We want to sit down and get this thing wrapped up and get on with this," said the official, who asked not to be identified.

Dole's forces acknowledged that Campbell was busy on Wednesday afternoon but said it was Kantor who had scheduling problems on Thursday and Friday, leaving Saturday as the next possible meeting date. "If there were any restraints put down on this early, it was with Kantor's schedule," one Dole campaign official said. "We are anxious to meet, and we are the ones proposing more debates."
Campbell's spokeswoman, Ginny Bueno, said he was in a board meeting of the American Council of Life Insurance, where he is president.

The first debate had been tentatively scheduled by the Commission on Presidential Debates for Sept. 25 -- next week -- in St. Louis, Missouri, but Clinton's aides have said he cannot participate that night because of a speech he is scheduled to give at the United Nations the day before.

"Our position remains the same. We're anxious to debate. We're anxious and ready to go, starting in St. Louis on the 25th or 26th (of September)," said Dole spokesman Nelson Warfield, who was travelling with the candidate in California.
"It's certainly clear that we want to reach out to the supporters of Ross Perot even if that candidate isn't in the debate," Warfield said.
Kantor said on Tuesday his side wanted two presidential and one vice presidential debate, all between Oct. 6-13. He said he was still pressing for Perot to be included.

The Dole campaign wants three presidential and one vice presidential debate, each 75 minutes long and with a single moderator, and all excluding Perot and his vice presidential running mate, Pat Choate.
